text: San Miguel de Sema is a town and municipality in the Boyacá Department of Colombia, situated within the Western Boyacá Province and one of the 123 municipalities of the department. Located to the west of Boyacá, it has an urban center at an altitude of 2,615 metres (8,579 ft) and is bordered by the municipalities of Chiquinquirá, Simijaca, Fúquene (in Cundinamarca), and the Boyacá municipalities Ráquira and Tinjacá. The name San Miguel de Sema combines the Spanish name for the archangel Saint Michael with the name of a pre-Columbian tribe, Sema or Semita. The area, part of the Chiquinquirá-Ubaté valley, was historically inhabited by the Muisca, who lived in a loose confederation, with governance of San Miguel de Sema carried out by a cacique of Chiquinquirá who remained loyal to the zaque based in Hunza. The town was founded on November 8, 1915, and officially recognized as a municipality in 1960. In 1925, a group of judges established the paths of old cattle ranches, including Sirigay, Quintone, and Peñablanca. Luis Alberto Ospina led the municipality's creation and, until his death, his children continued the foundational process that culminated in 1960. The primary economic activity is milk cattle ranching, particularly involving Holstein cattle, with production so significant that several companies producing milk derivatives have set up storage facilities. Agricultural activities, mainly in potatoes and corn, still persist in certain areas. The church dedicated to Saint Michael the Archangel (San Miguel Arcángel) is considered one of the most beautiful in the department. San Miguel de Sema provides access to Lake Fúquene. The municipality hosts fairs and celebrations during the second week of November, specifically on the 10th, 11th, and 12th, featuring bull and horse races and bovine shows, with San Miguel Arcángel as its patronal saint. Its geographic coordinates are 5°33′N 73°45′W (5.55°N 73.75°W).
